title: Fight Club
events_chronological: An insomniac car-recall investigator finds that the only thing that lets him sleep is crying at support groups for diseases he does not have.
Marla Singer starts attending the same groups, and her obvious faking destroys his release.
On a business flight the narrator meets soap salesman Tyler Durden and pockets his card.
The narrator's condo and all his catalogue furniture are destroyed in an explosion, and he calls Tyler, who takes him into a derelict house on Paper Street.
Outside a bar Tyler asks the narrator to hit him as hard as he can, and the two beat each other bloody in the car park.
The fights become a weekly basement club with its own rules, drawing in more and more men.
Marla overdoses, Tyler brings her back to Paper Street, and the two begin a loud affair the narrator cannot stand.
Tyler renders fat stolen from a liposuction clinic into soap and sells it back to the department stores at eighty dollars a bar.
Tyler burns the narrator's hand with lye and holds him there, refusing to let him retreat into meditation.
The narrator blackmails his boss into paying him to stay away, using his own beaten face as the evidence.
Tyler turns fight club into Project Mayhem, filling the house with shaven recruits who take orders and vandalise corporate property.
Tyler steers the car into oncoming traffic, lets it roll, and then disappears.
Project Mayhem member Robert Paulson is shot dead on an operation, and the narrator starts trying to shut the project down.
Travelling city to city, the narrator finds fight clubs everywhere and men who greet him as Tyler Durden.
The narrator works out that he and Tyler are the same person, and that Tyler has been acting while he sleeps.
Marla confirms that she has been sleeping with him, not with a separate man.
The narrator discovers that Project Mayhem has mined the credit-card company towers and tries to defuse the charges.
Tyler beats him down a stairwell in one of the towers, and the narrator puts a gun in his own mouth and shoots himself through the cheek to kill Tyler.
Marla is delivered to the tower by the Space Monkeys, and the two hold hands at the window as the buildings come down.
syuzhet_notes: Told-order bullet 1 is a flash-forward to the climax, with a gun already in the narrator's mouth, and the film catches up with it at told-order bullet 18. Everything between runs strictly forward. The film's nonlinearity is not reordering but unreliable narration: at told-order bullet 16 it replays earlier scenes with Tyler edited out, rewriting what the audience has already been shown rather than moving it in time.
fabula_notes: Every scene involving Tyler is, in story-world terms, the narrator acting alone, so this chronology records what happens rather than what is depicted. The destruction of the narrator's condo is revealed only much later to have been his own work.
